INTEREST OF THE AMICUS CURIAE1
Amicus curiae America’s Future, founded in 1946, is one of America’s oldest
public policy nonprofit organizations. It is exempt from federal income tax under
section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code. America’s Future participates in the
public policy process, including conducting research, and informing and educating
the public on the proper construction of state and federal constitutions, as well as
statutes related to the rights of citizens, and questions related to human and civil
rights secured by law. 
STATEMENT OF THE CASE
On January 20, 2025, President Trump issued Executive Order 14168,
“Defending Women From Gender Ideology Extremism and Restoring Biological
Truth to the Federal Government.” 90 FR 8615 (Jan. 30, 2025) (“the EO”). Section
1 of the EO recited: 
[I]deologues who deny the biological reality of sex have increasingly
used legal and other socially coercive means to permit men to
self-identify as women and gain access to intimate single-sex spaces
and activities designed for women, from women's domestic abuse
shelters to women’s workplace showers. This is wrong. Efforts to
eradicate the biological reality of sex fundamentally attack women by
depriving them of their dignity, safety, and well-being. [Id.] 
Section 2 declared, “It is the policy of the United States to recognize two sexes, male
and female. These sexes are not changeable and are grounded in fundamental and
incontrovertible reality.” Section 4(a) provided, “The Attorney General and
1
 It is hereby certified that no counsel for a party authored this brief in whole
or in part; and that no person other than this amicus curiae, its members, or its 
counsel made a monetary contribution to its preparation or submission.

2
Secretary of Homeland Security shall ensure that males are not detained in
women’s prisons or housed in women’s detention centers....” Finally, relevant here,
Section 4(c) provided that, “[t]he Attorney General shall ensure that the Bureau of
Prisons revises its policies concerning medical care to be consistent with this order,
and shall ensure that no Federal funds are expended for any medical procedure,
treatment, or drug for the purpose of conforming an inmate’s appearance to that of
the opposite sex.”
Consistent with the EO, the Federal Bureau of Prisons (“the Bureau” or
“BOP”), in memoranda dated February 21, 2025 and February 28, 2025, stated that
prisons must issue undergarments to prisoners consistent with their biological sex,
and that “no Bureau ... funds are to be expended for any medical procedure,
treatment, or drug for the purpose of conforming an inmate's appearance to that of
the opposite sex.” Kingdom v. Trump, 2025 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 105237 at *5-6
(D.D.C. 2025) (“Kingdom I”). Three inmates identifying as “transgender”
challenged the rule against opposite-sex underwear and cross-sex hormone
treatments, but not the prohibition on cross-sex surgical procedures. Id. at *12-13. 
On June 3, 2025, the district court for the District of Columbia issued a
preliminary injunction against the Bureau’s policy. The Court ruled that the
plaintiffs were likely to succeed on the merits of their Administrative Procedure Act
(“APA”) claim that the policy was arbitrary and capricious. The court ruled that
“neither the BOP nor the Executive Order provides any serious explanation” for the
change in policy, and the policy was therefore arbitrary and capricious. Id. at *35.

3
The court certified a broad class defined as “all persons who are currently or will be
incarcerated in BOP facilities with a current diagnosis of gender dysphoria or who
receive such a diagnosis in the future.” Id. at *43-44. The district court extended
its initial injunction against the Bureau three times: on August 20, 2025 (Kingdom
v. Trump, 2025 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 274377 (D.D.C. 2025)); on November 17, 2025
(Kingdom v. Trump, 2025 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 274376 (D.D.C. 2025)); and on February
12, 2026 (Kingdom v. Trump, 2026 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 33760 (D.D.C. 2026)). 
On February 19, 2026, BOP issued Program Statement 5260.01,
“Management of Inmates with Gender Dysphoria,” (“Program Statement”) which
superseded the original Implementing Memoranda. The Program Statement
“provide[d for] only psychotherapy and psychotropic medication to treat gender
dysphoria.” Kingdom v. Trump, 2026 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 135103 (D.D.C. 2026) at *4
(“Kingdom II”). On June 17, 2026 the district court issued a preliminary injunction
against the updated policy. Id. at *5, *50. That same day a D.C. Circuit panel
granted the Government a stay pending appeal. Kingdom v. Trump, 2026 U.S. App.
LEXIS 17585 (D.C. Cir. 2026). The D.C. Circuit ruled that 
[t]he Government is likely to succeed on the merits at bare minimum
because the district court's order appears to have been an
administrative injunction. There does not appear to be any
“discernible legal basis ... for issuing administrative injunctions,”
especially not in cases like this one involving the Prison Litigation
Reform Act. [Id. at *2-3.]

4
The court likewise found that the Government is “irreparably harmed by an
improper intrusion by a federal court into the workings of a coordinate branch of the
Government.” Id. at *3 (internal quotation omitted). 
On August 26, 2026, the district court reissued its preliminary injunction. 
Kingdom v. Trump, 2026 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 210805 (D.D.C. 2026). On appeal, on
September 18, 2026, a different D.C. Circuit split panel refused to stay the
injunction. The panel found the Government failed to show a likelihood of success
on the merits “because the Bureau of Prisons ... did not adequately consider its own
experience providing gender-affirming care under its prior policy.” Kingdom v.
Trump, 2026 U.S. App. LEXIS 28756 (D.C. Circuit) at *4 (“Kingdom III ”). In
dissent, Judge Walker argued that “[t]he government is likely to succeed on the
merits because the district court lacks the authority to reissue the 90-day
preliminary injunction first issued on June 17.... [T]he practice of issuing rolling
injunctions exceeds the limits imposed on courts by the Prison Litigation Reform
Act.” Id. at *6 (Walker, J., dissenting) (internal quotation omitted). 
STATEMENT
In Kingdom II, District Judge Lamberth made the intriguing statement that
“the Court has no intention of wading into the culture war being waged against
transgender individuals.” Id. at *5. Yet in that “culture war” of which Judge
Lamberth spoke, the “transgender” movement is hardly on the defensive. Rather,

5
at every societal stratum, the social contagion of “transgenderism” has been
assaulting the foundations of American society. 
Now, America’s correctional facilities are in the crosshairs of the transgender
advocates who want the American taxpayer to pay for, and BOP employees be
compelled to facilitate, experimentation on prisoners with mental conditions to see
if man can defy nature itself. To accomplish that goal, transgender advocates have
created an artificial and amorphous “class” that defies definition or verification. 
Justice Alito noted in a recent concurring opinion: 
The parties in this case also admit that transgender status is not an
immutable characteristic.... Instead, a person’s gender identity may
“shif[t],” and a person who is transgender now may not be transgender
later.... A person’s “gender identity” is an “internal sense,” ... and
transgender persons as a class do not uniformly “exhibit obvious,
immutable, or distinguishing characteristics that define them as a
discrete group.... Finally, the definition of transgender status ...
encompasses not just biological men who permanently identify as
women and biological women who permanently identify as men, but
also individuals who might identify with a particular gender at
a particular point in time and individuals who identify
permanently or temporarily with both sexes, neither sex, or
some other identity. [United States v. Skrmetti, 605 U.S. 495, 576-
577 (2025) (Alito, J., concurring) (emphasis added).] 
Transgender advocates can and do embrace this loose definition, but forcing
it on the Bureau of Prisons, which must make very real, very difficult decisions in
managing some of the most violent, difficult and lawless members of society, creates
an utterly untenable situation. BOP is responsible not only for keeping society safe
from its charges, but keeping its charges safe from one another. Prisons across
America are dealing with an epidemic of inmate sexual assaults, which leave very

6
real and definable people with very real and quantifiable injuries. The Bureau
faces extremely difficult facts and objective truths every day — facts and truths
which cannot be whitewashed by changing meaningful terminology into nonsensical
Newspeak. Simply renaming a group of men, some of whom are violent sexual
predators, as “transgender women” does not change who they are. Placing some of
the most dangerous biological men among us in the midst of a captive audience of
women, which some support, has been shown to make prisons a target-rich
environment for abuse. 
Thus, the effort by the cult of transgenderism to rewrite the lexicon, to
interpret definitions out of meaningful existence, and to deny all objective reality,
leaves in its wake a long trail of damaged human beings who may not know how
their attacker “identifies” that day, but cannot deny they have been violated and
devastated.
If there is any citadel that ought to quest for truth, to search for the actual
facts, to offer a place where the injured can seek a remedy, it is the courts of law. 
When the courts adopt the cult of transgenderism, insist on “exhibit[ing] a naivete
from which ordinary citizens are free,”2 and deny the very existence of objective
truth or historical fact, society’s race to the bottom must be near complete.
This case presents a stark reminder of why courts historically grant
deference to prison authorities to conduct day-to-day operations. Novel and
2
 Dept. of Corrections v. New York, 588 U.S. 752, 785 (2019).

7
factually-unrooted theories are of little value there. “Running a prison is an
inordinately difficult undertaking which requires expertise, planning, and the
commitment of resources, all of which are peculiarly within the province of
the legislative and executive branches of government.” Turner v. Safley, 482
U.S. 78, 84-85 (1987) (emphasis added). This is why this Court has held that even
where constitutional rights of prisoners are implicated, “the regulation is valid if it
is reasonably related to legitimate penological interests.” Id. at 89. 
SUMMARY OF ARGUMENT
The Bureau’s policy change is a legitimate penological judgment, wellgrounded in scientific, biological and criminological reality. As such, the courts
should defer to that judgment and the Bureau is likely to prevail on the merits. 
The Biden Administration transgender policies have been eclipsed by
exposure of the World Professional Association for Transgender Health (“WPATH”)
organization on which they relied as a political, not medical organization. The
transgender craze is passing, and science and reason are being restored.
Should the courts defer to the politics of “transgenderism” with respect to
hormones and underwear, the courts will be on the slippery slope of determining
whether to also meet similar demands for transgender surgery and putting
biological men in housing and cells with women. That has been tried in prisons,
putting female inmates at substantial risk.
It is difficult to conceive of a worse place to practice social experimentation in
the name of a radical ideology than a prison. This amicus urges this Court to

8
reverse the D.C. Circuit, to find that the Bureau is likely to succeed on the merits,
since the policy is doubtless “reasonably related to legitimate penological interests,”
and to find that the Government has an interest not only in the operation of its
laws, but in the protection of the lives and rights of those it has undertaken to
incarcerate, which are irreparably harmed by the injunction below.
ARGUMENT
I. THE BUREAU OF PRISONS POLICY CHANGE IS WELL
GROUNDED, ALTHOUGH AT VARIANCE WITH THE POLICY
PREFERENCES OF THE CIRCUIT COURT PANEL’S MAJORITY.
The D.C. Circuit’s per curiam opinion denying the Government’s motion for
stay concludes that “Appellants have not shown a strong likelihood of success on the
question of whether Program Statement 5260.01 is arbitrary and capricious
because the Bureau of Prisons (BOP) did not adequately consider its own experience
providing gender-affirming care under its prior policy.” Kingdom III at *4. Rather
than providing a meaningful discussion of why the Program Statement is “arbitrary
and capricious,” it runs together string cites about relying on inappropriate factors,
failing to consider important aspects of the problem and ignoring relevant evidence. 
The single illustration that it provides is that “BOP makes claims about the
security impact of providing gender-affirming care without addressing whether
such issues have occurred.” Id. (emphasis added). The very use of the term
“gender-affirming care” demonstrates that the panel majority embraces the
language of transgenderism. Rather clearly, the panel majority faults the Trump
Administration for changing the policies of the Biden Administration, as it

9
sanctions the district court injunction which preserves Biden Administration
policies well almost halfway into the Trump Administration. 
In dissent, Judge Walker explains exactly what Biden Administration
“gender-affirming care” has done previously, and how it would change: 
First, the BOP will no longer provide “sex trait modification surgeries.”
Second, the BOP will not start inmates on hormone therapy, and each
inmate currently receiving hormones will begin an individualized
“tapering plan.” Third, the BOP will no longer provide “social
accommodations” like makeup and wigs, and “when practicable,” the
BOP will “remove or confiscate the social accommodations” previously
provided. [Id. at *5-6.] 
The Application also explains that BOP no longer would provide “sex-traitmodification surgeries, hormone interventions in general, and social
accommodations ... as treatment for gender dysphoria....” and BOP provides the
reasons. Application for Stay (“App.”) at 1-2. Disproving the criticism by the D.C.
Circuit panel majority, one reason for the change was that those interventions did
not reflect the latest scientific information, which had undermined BOP’s prior
reliance on the recommendations of WPATH. This amicus filed an amicus brief in
United States v. Skrmetti, 605 U.S. 495 (2025)3 detailing why WPATH is not a
medical organization and cannot be relied upon. Justice Thomas explained at
length in his concurring opinion that WPATH is a political and profit-making
entity. See Skrmetti at 537-40, 543-46 (Thomas, J., concurring).
3
 See U.S. Supreme Court, No. 23-477, Brief of Amici Curiae America’s
Future, et al. (Oct. 15, 2024)

10
Unlike the political policy operating during the Biden Administration, the
current BOP judgment is well-grounded in basic human biology as understood by
nearly all thoughtful people in medicine, science, and laypeople until about 15 years
ago. As President Trump put it in his Executive Order 14168, there are “two sexes,
male and female. These sexes are not changeable and are grounded in fundamental
and incontrovertible reality.” And as Justice Thomas put it in a recent concurrence,
“Men and boys with gender dysphoria are not women or girls, even if they believe
that they are. Sex is an immutable ‘biological’ characteristic, ... it is binary; and
‘man’ and ‘woman,’ ‘boy’ and ‘girl,’ are the terms that correspond to adults and
children of each sex.” West Virginia v. B.P.J., 146 S. Ct. 2356, 2382 (2026) (Thomas,
J., concurring). As Justice Thomas noted correctly, “[t]o use language to obscure
reality — to show ‘indifference regarding the truth’ — is to lie to the public and
cease to treat our fellow citizens ‘as equal[s].’” Id. (emphasis added). In an earlier
and less politicized time, the position of BOP would be a universal truism akin to
saying “the sky is blue” or “water is composed of two hydrogen atoms and one
oxygen atom.” Unfortunately, the district court and the panel majority embraced a
political agenda less respectful of objective truth. For example, referring to the
concerns of one of the Plaintiffs, District Judge Lamberth wrote this selfcontradictory sentence, “Mr. Nichols states that he is ‘very scared to live without
testosterone therapy,’ fearing that he will lose muscle mass and start menstruating
again....” Kingdom I at *11. “Mr.” Nichols must be a woman. No man in human
history has experienced menstruation. The court’s own language betrays the

11
inescapable scientific reality that “Mr. Nichols” is neither a “Mr.” nor a “he;” but
rather, is a “Ms.” and a “she.” When most Americans read such political statements
which defy common knowledge in judicial decisions, they lost respect for the federal
courts. 
The great Russian dissident Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn wrote, “The simple step
of a courageous individual is not to take part in the lie.”4 The courts below have
“lie[d] to the public,” as Justice Thomas put it. This Court should not take part.
The BOP has no general obligation to provide elective medical treatments to
prisoners.5 Plaintiffs are demanding an exception to that rule by claiming that
their feelings or beliefs about themselves — which allow them to assume
“transgender status” — give them a specialized legal status, entitling them to
expensive elective procedures. 
As this Court recognized last year, “[d]isplaying passport holders’ sex at birth
no more offends equal protection principles than displaying their country of birth —
in both cases, the Government is merely attesting to a historical fact without
subjecting anyone to differential treatment.” Trump v. Orr, 146 S. Ct. 44, 46
(2025). Indeed, the fact is both historical and scientific. 
4
 Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn, The Gulag Archipelago.
5

12
As biologists Colin Wright and Emma Hilton note, the division of the human
race into two sexes, male and female, is a scientific fact which, like gravity, defies
political attempts to redefine reality.
[Some argue that] the categories male and female exist on a
“spectrum,” and are therefore no more than “social constructs.” To
characterize this line of reasoning as having no basis in reality would
be an egregious understatement. It is false at every conceivable
scale.... In humans ... an organism’s biological sex corresponds to one
of two distinct types of reproductive anatomy that develop for the
production of small or large sex cells — sperm and eggs, respectively —
and associated biological functions in sexual reproduction....
[R]eproductive anatomy is unambiguously male or female at birth
more than 99.98% of the time…. No third type of sex cell exists in
humans, and therefore there is no sex “spectrum” or additional sexes
beyond male and female. Sex is binary.6
As one research scholar writes: “the objective truth is that sex in humans is
strictly binary and immutable, for fundamental reasons that are common
knowledge to all biologists taking the findings of their discipline seriously. Denying
that sex in humans is binary attacks the very foundations of biological sciences.”7
As Virginia M. Miller, a professor emerita and former Director of the
Women's Health Research Center at the Mayo Clinic, has written, “Every cell has
a sex, which is determined by the presence of the complement of sex

chromosomes.”8 Science has proven that there are “underlying differences in
biology of the sexes. This conclusion should not be surprising given that every cell

The American College of Pediatricians has likewise emphasized the biological
reality that humanity is scientifically divided into two sexes. As doctors Michael
Artigues and Michelle Cretella note, 
[s]ex is a dimorphic, innate trait defined in relation to an organism’s
biological role in reproduction.... [P]rimary sex determination occurs at
fertilization and is directed by a complement of sex determining genes
on the X and Y chromosomes.… Consideration of these innate
differences is critical to the practice of good medicine and to the
development of sound public policy for children and adults alike.9 
“The National Institutes of Health urges scientists and physicians to include
sex as a biological variable in all aspects of healthcare. [T]he reality of sexual
dimorphism and its importance to health has been documented for decades.” Id.
Pediatricians do not “assign” an infant’s sex; they announce it based
upon the physical reality of the infant’s body.... This growing
movement to deny the physical reality of sexual dimorphism requires a
dangerous dismissal of both science and medical ethics, one that will
cause severe harm to individuals and society at large if embraced. [Id.]

9

14
 Scientists do not “assign” to water the property of having two hydrogen
atoms and one oxygen atom. They simply recognize the fact that it does. And
“[i]nterventions that alter a person’s sexual appearance do not alter the person’s
genetic code. Therefore, sex does not change. Administering sex hormones and
other drugs ... do not change biological sex.” Id.
The “transgender lexicon” is the theater of the absurd. As the Fifth Circuit
recently noted, in denying the motion of a male federal prisoner to require prison
employees to refer to him by a female name and pronouns:
“[s]ome transgender people may request ... more unfamiliar pronouns,
such as ze (pronounced ‘zee’) and hir (pronounced ‘hear’)).” If a court
orders one litigant referred to as “her” (instead of “him”), then the
court can hardly refuse when the next litigant moves to be referred to
as “xemself ” (instead of “himself”). Deploying such neologisms could
hinder communication among the parties and the court.... When local
governments have sought to enforce pronoun usage, they have had to
make refined distinctions based on matters such as the types of
allowable pronouns and the intent of the “misgendering” offender....
Courts would have to do the same. We decline to enlist the federal
judiciary in this quixotic undertaking. [United States v. Varner,
948 F.3d 250, 257-58 (5th Cir. 2020) (emphasis added).]
Even proponents of the transgender delusion cannot define their own terms. 
A Texas state representative made the utterly unscientific and utterly false
statement that there are “six really common biological sexes.... The point is that
biologically speaking, scientifically speaking, sex is a spectrum, and oftentimes can
be very ambiguous.”10
 But that’s just the sexes. When it comes to “genders,” we are

now told there are far more — though we are not told exactly how many. In one
recent survey, the Trevor Project reported that “LGBTQ youth in the survey
identified with more than 100 gender identities.”11 Included in that dizzying,
undefined and almost certainly undefinable array were such categories as
transfemme, agenderflux, two spirited, demi-boy, neutrois, and trigender. Id.
As the BOP notes, the “science” behind the transgender mania has been
effectively debunked, with scientists finally beginning to publicly concede the
obvious. And it is perhaps little wonder that scientists are now admitting that
gender dysphoria rarely occurs alone. It is generally one of many associated mental
health co-morbidities that call the basis for the subjective impressions of the patient
even more into question. As one example, a recent study in the European Journal
of Pediatrics noted that in young people with gender dysphoria, “an
over-representation of comorbidities exists, notably mental health disorders and
autistic spectrum disorder.”12 These mental health disorders included
“depression..., anxiety..., eating disorder[s].... borderline personality disorder ... and
emotionally unstable personality disorder.” Id. at 2971. “Anxiety, eating disorders,
depression, self-harm and suicidal ideation have been well documented in

adolescents and adults with [gender dysphoria]..., with a much higher than the

II. THE BUREAU OF PRISONS HAS MADE THE LEGITIMATE
PENOLOGICAL JUDGMENT THAT IT DOES NOT WISH TO
POTENTIALLY INFLICT LIFELONG HARM TO INMATES WITH
PSYCHOLOGICAL PROBLEMS UNDER ITS CARE. 
At the core of the transgender mania that swept the nation over the past
several years is the notion that a person was born in the wrong body, and seeks to
have the body of the opposite sex. Reduced to simple terms, this is a mental
condition that often drives one to ask physicians to remove healthy tissue (e.g.,
breasts from women; penises from men) in procedures which are largely or
completely irreversible. Fortunately, there is reason to believe this mania has run
its course and sanity is returning. As the Bureau notes, surgical and hormone
treatments to address a mental health condition are, somewhat intuitively perhaps,
“highly controversial, medically disputed, and unproven.” App. at 26. It made the
utterly reasonable decision to instead prioritize “the psychotherapeutic model [a]s
the most appropriate treatment model.” Id. This decision is for the Bureau to
make, and it is entirely proper. 
The scientific profession is increasingly coming to the realization that ought
to be intuitive — cutting off healthy body parts or taking unnatural hormones
attempting to fight against nature — are hardly the best ways to address
discomfort with one’s sex, and in fact have significant and irreparable physical
harms. And those who today seek self-mutilation may tomorrow regret their

17
decisions. It is not difficult to imagine that the prisoners who today are demanding
drastic and unnatural hormone treatments will in the future regret their decision
and seek to hold the BOP legally and financially responsible for the “treatment” it
provided, much as minors today are seeking to hold to account the physicians and
psychiatrists who facilitated their injuries.
In February 2026, Fox Varian won the first jury verdict by a “detransitioner”
against the doctor and psychologist who recommended and performed the removal
of her healthy breasts at 16 years old, awarding her a $2 million verdict.13 “I was
16, and I was really, really mentally ill, obviously,” Varian testified. “I obviously
wasn’t mature enough to make the decision to have surgery, and I certainly wasn't
mature enough to handle the aftermath.” Id. Might not a prisoner take this
position after receiving the treatment he or she desires?
Chloe Cole also underwent a double mastectomy, at just 15 years old.14 Cole
noted that she became suicidal after the surgery, not before. “When my
specialist first told my parents that they could have a dead daughter or a live
transgender son, I wasn’t suicidal. I was a happy child who struggled because she
was different,” she said. “However, at 16, after my surgery, I did become suicidal. 
I’m doing better now. But my parents almost got the dead daughter promised to

them by my doctors.... My doctors had almost created the very nightmare they said

Soren Aldaco is a Texas woman who also began hormone treatments at 17
and had a double mastectomy at 19.15 She too is suing her doctors and counselors:
